desc: Parse N, W, intervals, Q, queries.

Build overlap graph H components using segment tree + DSU: for each interval, insert its index into segment tree nodes covering [L,R], then DFS on segment tree unioning all indices in the same node and between parent-child.

Count number of H-components. If ≥2, precompute for each component its minimum weight. For queries: if s,t in different components, answer = W_s + W_t; else answer = W_s + W_t + min_weight_outside_component(s).

If H has exactly 1 component, compute G components: build interval order poset by finding immediate left (max R < L_i) and immediate right (min L > R_i) neighbors using sorted sweeps and segment trees, then union these edges to get G components.

For each G component, precompute prefix/suffix minimums of W to answer queries: if s,t disjoint -> W_s+W_t; else if they intersect but in same G component -> W_s+W_t + min(left_min(min(L_s,L_t)), right_min(max(R_s,R_t))); else -1.
Test on sample inputs and edge cases.
Verify the diameter ≤2 assumption with more edge cases, especially for complex interval orders.
Consider if the Hasse diagram might miss some connections (should be fine as it's a spanning forest of the comparability graph).

Fix the bug in the random testing framework where it incorrectly reported 'All tests passed!' without properly comparing results, and ensure the test loop actually runs and prints mismatches. Also verify that the fast solution handles the case when H is connected but G has multiple components correctly.
After fixing the testing framework, run extensive random tests (N up to 10, 1000+ cases) to ensure the fast solution always matches brute force.
If mismatches are found, debug the algorithm (likely in the Hasse diagram construction or the prefix/suffix minimum logic for the connected H case).
Once tests pass, clean up the code and ensure it reads from stdin and writes to stdout as required.
